title: Ten thousand nodes, ten thousand meshes and ten thousand named materials

criterion.says: Node, mesh, primitive and texture count performance test

acceptanceClass.because: The framing rule's own direction over a static subject. What is compared is which pixels each side covers and which material's colour each wears there.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: NodePerformanceTest
subjects.notes: Attributes NORMAL, POSITION. KHR_lights_punctual. Ten thousand materials, every one of them named.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [-146.9078816003247, -17.37695625682049, -146.1362344263198] to [145.61308917899316, 16.388933535798657, 146.60660985945944], so centre = [-0.6473962106657751, -0.49401136051091576, 0.2351877165698255] and radius = 207.60962558350337 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 1482.6741444073666, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius.
camera.note: The glTF carries no camera, so the framing rule supplies one. Roll is 0 because the rule sets it: a roll chosen here and nowhere else would make this subject's placement a second determination competing with the rule.

light.note: The material emits, so nothing has to arrive for the picture to exist.

world.note: Declared and zero rather than left factory, so the picture is a function of this manifest and not of a Blender default.

material.note: Emission, one colour per glTF material, from a RULE with no free parameter rather than from a table: colour[c] = 0.15 + 0.70 * frac(index * step[c]). A table names materials and is right while a subject draws a handful; past that it is a transcription of the file. The rule takes no parameter, so a manifest cannot tune a colour to make a case pass (board:1362).

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. At one sample per pixel of a deterministic emission there is nothing for a seed to change, so any pixel that moves between these two renders is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us -- which is what makes this the instrument floor instead of an assumption about it.

notes: A coverage case. Its shading -- textures, metallic-roughness, any extension it declares -- is NOT what this decides; board:1363 records why no case takes the shading arm yet. IT IS A COST CASE UPSTREAM OF BEING A PICTURE CASE, and what it first decides is that ten thousand nodes resolve and draw at all. A colour table for it would be ten thousand declared triples, which is the argument for the rule made at its limit.

subjectFrameFraction.note: PLACEHOLDER, and said to be one: no run has recomputed a fraction for this case yet, so there was nothing to seed it from (board:1377).
